mainTopic: The באר הקר, and a dead שרץ found in the מקדש: how and from where to remove it, and whether bringing a שרץ into the מקדש is חייב.
overview: This amud opens by finishing a story from the previous amud. A Sage allowed a water-wheel to be used, but forbade it once he saw people soaking flax in the water. The גמרא then asks what the באר הקר in the משנה is. שמואל's explanation, 'a well they argued about and permitted', is rejected because a ברייתא speaks of many such wells. רב נחמן בר יצחק explains instead that it is a well of fresh spring water, and the full ברייתא adds that the permission came from an old custom of their fathers. A new משנה follows about a dead שרץ found in the מקדש on שבת. It records two disputes: how to remove the שרץ (belt or wooden tongs) and from which areas it must be removed (only the inner areas, or the whole עזרה). It closes with רבי שמעון's rule that such leniencies only override a שבות. In the גמרא, שמואל rules that bringing the שרץ itself into the מקדש is פטור, based on the פסוק 'מזכר ועד נקבה תשלחו'. The גמרא then tests whether the תנאים of the משנה disagree about this question, first with the belt-versus-tongs dispute and then with the dispute about which areas the שרץ must be removed from.

steps.title: The flax-soaking ending of the wheel story
steps.stepSummary: The story from the previous section ends. Once people were found soaking flax in the water, the Sage forbade them to use the wheel.
steps.simpleTranslation: They were soaking flax in it, so he forbade them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a story that started on the previous amud. A Sage had permitted drawing water with a wheel, but when he saw people soaking flax in that water, he took the permission back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The permission depended on the water being drawn for permitted uses like drinking. Soaking flax is ordinary work that is not allowed, so using the wheel might lead people to draw water for a forbidden purpose. Because the use changed, the ruling changed.

keyTerms.meaning: They soaked or steeped (in water)
Flax
He forbade them

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a היתר can depend on how people actually use something. If the use becomes problematic, the permission can be withdrawn.

phrases.english: They were soaking flax in it —
phrases.notes: 'בַּהּ' refers to the water, or the place where the wheel drew water, from the story on the previous amud.

phrases.english: he forbade them.
phrases.notes: He forbade drawing water with the wheel.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּרוּ בַּהּ כִּיתָּנָא אֲסַר לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the wheel story begun on the previous amud.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Once the water was being used for a forbidden purpose (soaking flax), the permission to use the wheel was withdrawn.

steps.title: What is the באר הקר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next phrase of the משנה, 'ומבאר הקר', and asks what kind of well this is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said, 'and from the באר הקר.' What is the באר הקר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new phrase in the משנה and asks for its meaning. This question sets up the explanations that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allows drawing water from the באר הקר on יום טוב, but the name is unclear. The גמרא wants to know what the word 'הקר' means and which well it refers to.

keyTerms.meaning: The באר הקר, a well mentioned in the משנה
What is?

steps.confusionAlert: This question starts a new topic. It is not part of the flax story; it goes back to a different phrase in the משנה.

phrases.english: "And from the Heker Well."
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה: one may draw water from it on יום טוב.

phrases.english: What is the Heker Well?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי בְּאֵר הַקַּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the wheel story to the next phrase in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the name 'באר הקר' and which well it refers to.

steps.title: שמואל: a well that was argued about and permitted
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains that the name comes from 'הקרו דברים': the Sages brought arguments about this well and permitted it.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: It is a pit about which they brought arguments, and they permitted it.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the question. He reads 'הקר' as coming from the word for presenting arguments, so this is the well the Sages debated and then permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to שמואל, the name is a nickname based on history. It is the one well that was the subject of a debate that ended with a היתר. That makes the name refer to one specific well.

keyTerms.meaning: They brought arguments about it
And they permitted it

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
a pit about which they brought arguments
phrases.notes: שמואל links 'הקר' to 'הקרו', bringing forward arguments.

phrases.english: and they permitted it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל בּוֹר שֶׁהִקְרוּ עָלֶיהָ דְּבָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: באר הקר is the one well that the Sages debated and then permitted for drawing water on יום טוב.

steps.title: A ברייתא speaks of many בורות הקרות
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says 'they did not permit all the בורות הקרות, only this one.' That means there are many 'קר' wells, which does not fit שמואל's history-based name.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: They did not permit all the בורות הקרות, only this one. If you say the name means 'they brought arguments about it', what does 'only this one' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל with a ברייתא. The ברייתא talks about 'בורות הקרות' in the plural, so the name must describe a kind of well, not one specific well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'הקר' meant 'the well they argued about', only one well would have that name, and saying 'not all בורות הקרות, only this one' would make no sense. The ברייתא assumes many wells share the name, and only one of them was permitted. So 'הקר' must describe some quality the wells have.

keyTerms.meaning: The Heker pits (plural)
Only this one
And if you say

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא does not disagree with the ruling that this well is permitted. The problem is only with שמואל's explanation of the name, since the plural shows the name describes a type of well.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
They did not permit all the Heker pits,
but only this one.
And if you say "that they brought arguments about it,"
what is the meaning of "only this one"?
phrases.notes: If the name belongs to one well, there are no other Heker wells to exclude.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי לֹא כׇּל הַבּוֹרוֹת הַקָּרוֹת הִתִּירוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks שמואל's explanation from step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's explanation that 'הקר' means 'they brought arguments about it'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא uses 'בורות הקרות' in the plural and says 'only this one', so the name is a category shared by many wells. That cannot fit a nickname based on the history of one well.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: a well of fresh spring water
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains instead that באר הקר means a well of מים חיים (fresh spring water), based on the פסוק 'כהקיר ביר מימיה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב נחמן בר יצחק said: It is a well of living (spring) water, as it says, 'As a well keeps its waters fresh...'
steps.whatsHappening: Because of the challenge, the גמרא drops שמואל's explanation. רב נחמן בר יצחק gives a new one: 'הקר' describes a well with fresh flowing water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in ירמיהו uses 'הקיר' for a well that keeps its water fresh, so 'הקר' describes a type of well. That fits the ברייתא: there are many spring-water wells, and only one of them was permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the earlier explanation and gives a new one)
Living water, meaning fresh spring water
As it keeps fresh (ירמיהו ו:ז)

steps.whatToRemember: באר הקר is a well of fresh spring water (מים חיים). שמואל's explanation, 'a well they argued about', was rejected because a ברייתא speaks of many בורות הקרות.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
a well of living (spring) water,
as it is stated:
"As a well keeps its waters fresh, etc."
phrases.notes: This is ירמיהו 6:7; the word 'הקיר' comes from the same root as 'הקר'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק בְּאֵר מַיִם חַיִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces שמואל's explanation, which the challenge in step 4 overturned.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A new explanation replaces the rejected one (introduced by אלא).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל: the name comes from the arguments made to permit one specific well.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'הקר' describes a type of well, one with fresh spring water. That allows many בורות הקרות, only one of which was permitted, as the ברייתא says.

steps.title: The full ברייתא about the one permitted well
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the whole ברייתא: only this one well was permitted, and the prophets permitted it to the returning exiles.
steps.simpleTranslation: Back to the ברייתא itself: They did not permit all the בורות הקרות, only this one. When the exiles came back from בבל they camped by it, and the prophets among them permitted it to them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back and quotes, in full, the ברייתא it used in the earlier question (Step 4). Now we hear the rest of its story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, only the first line was quoted. That line was used to show there are many 'קר' wells. Now we learn why this particular well was special: the returning exiles camped there, and the prophets of that time permitted them to use it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The matter itself.' The גמרא is returning to quote a source in full.
The exiles who returned from בבל to ארץ ישראל.
They camped by it.
Prophets. Here this means חגי, זכריה, and מלאכי.

phrases.english: The matter itself:
phrases.notes: This signals that a source quoted earlier is now being brought in full.

phrases.english: They did not permit all the Heker wells,
but only this one.
And when the exiles came up, they camped by it,
and the prophets among them permitted it to them.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא: לֹא כׇּל הַבּוֹרוֹת הַקָּרוֹת הִתִּירוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא from Step 4 and quotes the rest of it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only this one באר הקר was permitted, and the prophets permitted it to the returning exiles.

steps.title: It was really an old family custom
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא corrects itself: the permission did not start with the prophets. It was a custom the people already had from their fathers.
steps.simpleTranslation: Actually, it was not the prophets among them who permitted it. Rather, they had a custom from their fathers.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא fixes what it just said. The source of the permission was an old custom, not a new ruling by the prophets.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'ולא... אלא' ('not... rather') push aside the idea that the prophets made a new rule. The prophets only allowed the people to continue a practice they already had. This closes the באר הקר discussion.

keyTerms.meaning: Custom; an accepted practice.
Their fathers, meaning their ancestors.
'In their hands,' meaning they already had it.

steps.whatToRemember: באר הקר was a special case. Only this one well was permitted, and the permission came from an old custom of their fathers. The prophets simply allowed it to continue.

phrases.english: And not the prophets among them,
but rather, they had a custom of their fathers in their hands.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא נְבִיאִים שֶׁבֵּינֵיהֶן, אֶלָּא מִנְהַג אֲבוֹתָם בִּידֵיהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Corrects the claim in Step 6 that the prophets were the source of the permission.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only who started the permission is rejected. The permission itself stays.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Saying the prophets created the permission is not accurate. It was an older custom.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The well was permitted because of an ancestral custom, which the prophets approved.

steps.title: New משנה: a כהן removes a dead שרץ with his belt
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins. רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה says a כהן takes a dead שרץ out of the מקדש using his belt, so the טומאה is not left there.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If a dead שרץ is found in the מקדש on שבת, a כהן takes it out using his belt, so the טומאה does not stay there any longer. These are the words of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts here. It asks how to deal with a dead creeping animal, which makes things טמא, when it is found in the מקדש on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה's main concern is speed. The כהן should use his belt right away, even though the belt will become טמא. Getting the טומאה out of the מקדש quickly comes first.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מתניתין: 'our משנה.' This marks the start of a new משנה.
A dead creeping animal from the eight kinds listed in the תורה. It makes things טמא.
The belt, one of the כהן's special garments.
To let the טומאה stay longer.

steps.confusionAlert: Using the belt is not a way to avoid טומאה. The belt does become טמא. רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה accepts that, so that the שרץ can be removed faster.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A dead creeping animal that is found in the Temple —
a priest takes it out with his belt,
so as not to let the impurity stay longer,
these are the words of Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁרֶץ שֶׁנִּמְצָא בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ כֹּהֵן מוֹצִיאוֹ בְּהֶמְיָינוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the באר הקר discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Remove the שרץ right away with the belt, so the טומאה does not stay in the מקדש.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: use wooden tongs instead
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה disagrees. He says to use wooden tongs, so that no more טומאה is created.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: Take it out with wooden tongs, so as not to add more טומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה gives the opposite approach. He would rather use a tool that does not become טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is about which matters more. רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה cares about not delaying. רבי יהודה cares about not making more things טמא. A simple wooden tool like tongs cannot become טמא, so it keeps the belt clean.

keyTerms.meaning: Wooden tongs. A simple wooden tool that does not become טמא.
To add more טומאה, meaning to make more objects טמא.

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a classic clash between two values: speed (not leaving the טומאה) versus not spreading the טומאה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
with wooden tongs,
so as not to add more impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: בִּצְבַת שֶׁל עֵץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה about how to remove the שרץ.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Remove the שרץ with wooden tongs, so no new טומאה is created.

steps.title: Which areas must it be removed from?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks from which places in the מקדש the שרץ must be removed on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we take it out?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is setting up the next disagreement. It asks which areas are holy enough that the שרץ must be removed from them even on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a weekday it is obvious that the שרץ is removed from anywhere. The question is about שבת, when carrying it out is a problem. So the משנה asks where the holiness of the place makes removal necessary anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: From where?
We take out; we remove.

phrases.english: From where do we take it out?

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵהֵיכָן מוֹצִיאִין אוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from how to remove the שרץ to where it must be removed from.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which areas of the מקדש require removing the שרץ on שבת.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן ננס: only the holiest inner areas
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן ננס answers: from the היכל, the אולם, and the space between the אולם and the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the היכל, from the אולם, and from the area between the אולם and the מזבח. These are the words of רבי שמעון בן ננס.
steps.whatsHappening: The first answer lists only the very holiest inner areas.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי שמעון בן ננס's view, only these top-level holy places justify removing the שרץ on שבת. In the rest of the עזרה it is left where it is.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sanctuary building.
The Entrance Hall in front of the היכל.
The especially holy area between the Entrance Hall and the altar.

phrases.english: From the Sanctuary, and from the Entrance Hall,
and from between the Entrance Hall and the altar,
these are the words of Rabbi Shimon ben Nannas.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִן הַהֵיכָל, וּמִן הָאוּלָם, וּמִבֵּין הָאוּלָם וְלַמִּזְבֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Only the היכל, the אולם, and the area between the אולם and the מזבח.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: anywhere entering while טמא carries כרת
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says the שרץ must be removed from every place where entering while טמא carries כרת (or a חטאת if by mistake). In other places, it is covered with a bowl.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: From any place where someone who enters while טמא on purpose gets כרת, and by mistake brings a חטאת, we take it out. In all the other places, we cover it with a bowl.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא gives a wider rule. The test is whether entering that area while טמא is a כרת-level sin. Anywhere less holy, the שרץ is just covered until after שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of naming specific rooms, רבי עקיבא gives a general test. That test covers the whole עזרה, which is much more than רבי שמעון בן ננס's list. In the less holy areas, the שרץ is not removed on שבת. It is covered with a bowl so it is out of the way and people are less likely to touch it.

keyTerms.meaning: Doing it on purpose.
Spiritual cutting off; the punishment for certain sins done on purpose.
Doing it by mistake.
A sin-offering, brought for certain sins done by mistake.
A bowl or large vessel used to cover something.

steps.whatToRemember: There are two arguments in this משנה. HOW to remove the שרץ: belt (to be fast) versus wooden tongs (to avoid more טומאה). WHERE to remove it from: only the innermost areas (רבי שמעון בן ננס) versus anywhere entering while טמא carries כרת (רבי עקיבא). Everywhere else, cover it with a bowl.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁחַיָּיבִין עַל זְדוֹנוֹ כָּרֵת
phrases.english: Any place where one is liable to karet for entering on purpose
and to a sin-offering for entering by mistake —
from there we take it out.
And all the other places —
we turn a bowl over it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁחַיָּיבִין עַל זְדוֹנוֹ כָּרֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי שמעון בן ננס and gives a broader area.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Remove the שרץ from every area where entering while טמא carries כרת. In less holy areas, cover it with a bowl.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: The Sages only permitted rabbinic prohibitions
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון explains that the leniencies the חכמים allowed in the מקדש on שבת (like carrying out the שרץ) only permitted things that were rabbinic (שבות) prohibitions, not Torah prohibitions.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: wherever the חכמים permitted something to you, they gave you only from what was already yours, because they only permitted things that are forbidden as a שבות (a rabbinic rule).
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with רבי שמעון giving a general principle about all the שבת leniencies we just learned for the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים did not permit any Torah-level מלאכה. The things they allowed were only forbidden by rabbinic decree in the first place. So they were 'giving you from your own': they relaxed their own rule, not a Torah law.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic prohibition on שבת (not a Torah-level מלאכה)
They gave you from your own, meaning they relaxed only what was theirs to relax
They permitted

steps.whatToRemember: The חכמים' leniencies in the מקדש only override rabbinic rules (שבות), never Torah prohibitions.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
Wherever the Sages permitted something to you,
they gave it to you from your own,
phrases.notes: They only relaxed a rule that was theirs to begin with.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא הִתִּירוּ לְךָ אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם שְׁבוּת.
phrases.english: for they permitted to you only what is forbidden as a rabbinic decree.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: מָקוֹם שֶׁהִתִּירוּ לְךָ חֲכָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a general principle explaining the scope of the leniencies discussed in Steps 8-12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All the leniencies granted in the מקדש on שבת involve only rabbinic (שבות) prohibitions.

steps.title: שמואל: Bringing in something defiled by a שרץ is liable, the שרץ itself is exempt
steps.stepSummary: רב טבי בר קיסנא quotes שמואל: someone who brings an item made טמא by a שרץ into the מקדש is חייב, but someone who brings in the dead שרץ itself is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב טבי בר קיסנא said in the name of שמואל: one who brings into the מקדש something that became טמא from a שרץ is liable. One who brings in the שרץ itself is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a surprising ruling from שמואל about bringing טומאה into the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might expect the שרץ itself, which is the source of the טומאה, to be worse than an item it made טמא. שמואל rules the opposite: the item that became טמא brings liability, but the שרץ does not. This ties into our משנה about a שרץ found in the מקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: Something that became טמא by touching a dead שרץ
One who brings in
Liable to punishment (here, for breaking the command to send טומאה out of the camp)
Exempt

steps.confusionAlert: This is backwards from what you might expect. The source of the טומאה (the שרץ) is exempt, while what it made טמא brings liability.

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רַב טָבִי בַּר קִיסְנָא
phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav Tavi bar Kisna said
that Shmuel said:
One who brings into the Temple something defiled by a creeping animal is liable,
but if he brings in the creeping animal itself, he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב טָבִי בַּר קִיסְנָא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא with a new statement related to the משנה's topic of a שרץ in the מקדש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bringing an item made טמא by a שרץ into the מקדש brings liability. Bringing the שרץ itself does not.

steps.title: What is the reason for שמואל's distinction?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the שרץ itself should be exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of שמואל's surprising ruling. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the ruling sounds backwards, the גמרא needs a source that shows why the שרץ is excluded.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind Step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for exempting the שרץ itself.

steps.title: The verse applies only to what can be purified in a מקוה
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'מזכר ועד נקבה תשלחו' teaches that only things that can become טהור in a מקוה must be sent out. A שרץ can never become טהור, so it is excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'Both male and female shall you send out.' This means someone who can become טהור in a מקוה. That excludes a שרץ, which can never become טהור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק that limits the מצוה of sending the טמא out of the camp.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Male and female' refers to people, who can go to a מקוה and become טהור. So the מצוה only covers things that can be purified. A dead שרץ stays טמא forever, so bringing it in does not violate this מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: You shall send out (of the camp)
Purification by immersing in a מקוה
This excludes

steps.whyThisMatters: This derivation is the basis of שמואל's ruling. In steps 19–23 the גמרא checks whether the תנאים of our משנה disagree about exactly this question: is bringing a שרץ into the מקדש חייב or פטור?

phrases.english: The verse said:
"Both male and female shall you send out" (Numbers 5:3),
meaning one who can be purified in a ritual bath.
This excludes a creeping animal, which has no purification.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: מִזָּכָר וְעַד נְקֵבָה תְּשַׁלֵּחוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The obligation to send out applies only to what can become טהור in a מקוה. A שרץ cannot, so it is excluded.

steps.title: Attempted support from רבי יוסי הגלילי excluding an earthenware vessel
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that a ברייתא supports שמואל: רבי יוסי הגלילי uses the same פסוק to exclude a כלי חרס, apparently because a כלי חרס cannot be purified in a מקוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say a ברייתא supports him? 'Both male and female shall you send out' excludes an earthenware vessel. These are the words of רבי יוסי הגלילי. What is the reason? Is it not because it cannot be purified in a מקוה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to bring proof for שמואל's reasoning from a ברייתא that excludes a כלי חרס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כלי חרס that becomes טמא cannot be purified in a מקוה. It only stops being טמא when it breaks. If רבי יוסי הגלילי excludes it, the reason seems to be the same as שמואל's: no purification in a מקוה, so no מצוה to send it out.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say that this supports him?
An earthenware vessel
To the exclusion of
Is it not because...?

phrases.english: Let us say that a baraita supports him:
"Both male and female shall you send out"
excludes an earthenware vessel;
these are the words of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.
What is the reason?

phrases.aramaic: לָאו מִשּׁוּם דְּלֵית לֵיהּ טׇהֳרָה בְּמִקְוֶה?
phrases.english: Is it not because it has no purification in a ritual bath?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to support the reasoning of Step 16 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's principle that only things purifiable in a מקוה must be sent out.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוסי הגלילי's ברייתא excluding a כלי חרס from the same פסוק.

steps.title: Rejection: the reason may be that an earthenware vessel never becomes an אב הטומאה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. רבי יוסי הגלילי may hold that only something that can become an אב הטומאה is sent out, and a כלי חרס never becomes one.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. The verse means something that can become an אב הטומאה. That excludes an earthenware vessel, which never becomes an אב הטומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof by offering a different reason for רבי יוסי הגלילי's exclusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People and metal vessels can become an אב הטומאה (for example, through contact with a מת), but a כלי חרס cannot. So רבי יוסי הגלילי's exclusion may rest on this reason and not on purification in a מקוה. Because of that, the ברייתא does not prove שמואל's reasoning.

keyTerms.meaning: A primary source of טומאה, which can make other things טמא
No (the proof is rejected)

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's ruling stands on his own reading of the פסוק. The ברייתא about a כלי חרס does not prove it, because it can be explained by the אב הטומאה criterion.
steps.confusionAlert: Both reasons fit a כלי חרס, since it can't be purified in a מקוה and also can't become an אב הטומאה. That is exactly why the proof fails: we can't tell which reason רבי יוסי הגלילי meant.

phrases.english: No, it refers to something that can become a primary source of impurity.
This excludes an earthenware vessel,
which does not become a primary source of impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, מִי שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה אַב הַטּוּמְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof attempted in Step 17.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the ברייתא, not שמואל's ruling itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא's exclusion of a כלי חרס can be explained by a different reason: it never becomes an אב הטומאה.

steps.title: Proposing a תנאים dispute: belt or wooden tongs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that שמואל's ruling may be the subject of a תנאים dispute. It quotes a משנה about how a כהן removes a שרץ found in the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say this is like a dispute of תנאים: a שרץ found in the מקדש — a כהן takes it out with his belt, so as not to leave the טומאה there any longer. These are the words of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה. רבי יהודה says: he takes it out with wooden tongs, so as not to add more טומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It brings a משנה with two opinions, which it will soon connect to שמואל's question of whether bringing a שרץ into the מקדש is חייב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה wants the שרץ out as fast as possible, even if the כהן's belt becomes טמא. רבי יהודה prefers wooden tongs, which take longer to get but do not become טמא, so no new טומאה is created. The two opinions show two competing concerns: speed against avoiding extra טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say it is like a dispute between תנאים, a suggestion that an Amoraic question was already debated earlier
The belt of the כהן, one of the בגדי כהונה
Wooden tongs, which do not become טמא
To let the טומאה stay in the holy place for longer
To add more טומאה by making more items טמא

steps.confusionAlert: Both opinions agree that the שרץ must be taken out right away, even on שבת. They only argue about the method: the belt, which is fast but makes the belt טמא, or wooden tongs, which are slower but create no new טומאה.

phrases.english: Let us say it is like a dispute of Tannaim:
a dead creeping creature that is found in the Temple —
a priest takes it out with his belt,
phrases.notes: The belt is a priestly garment, and it will become impure.

phrases.english: so as not to let the impurity stay there longer,
these are the words of Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
he takes it out with wooden tongs,
so as not to add to the impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא כְּתַנָּאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof from רבי יוסי הגלילי was rejected, the גמרא tries a new source: a תנאים dispute.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's ruling that bringing the שרץ itself into the מקדש is פטור
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה with רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה and רבי יהודה about removing a שרץ from the מקדש

steps.title: Linking each opinion to חייב or פטור
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains how the משנה connects to שמואל. The one worried about delay holds that bringing in a שרץ is חייב, and the one worried about adding טומאה holds it is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't this what they argue about? The one who says 'so as not to delay' holds that one who brings a שרץ into the מקדש is חייב. The one who says 'so as not to add' holds that one who brings a שרץ into the מקדש is פטור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out exactly how the two opinions in the משנה would line up with the question of whether bringing a שרץ into the מקדש is חייב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If bringing in a שרץ is a real sin (חייב), then leaving it there is serious too, so it must come out as fast as possible, even with the belt. If bringing it in is פטור, there is no special rush, so it is better to avoid making the belt טמא. That would make רבי יהודה agree with שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it that... (introduces a suggested reading of a source)
They disagree
He holds
One who brings in

phrases.english: Isn't it that this is what they disagree about:
that the one who says 'so as not to delay'
holds: one who brings a creeping creature into the Temple is liable.
And the one who says 'so as not to add'
holds: one who brings a creeping creature into the Temple is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי לָאו, בְּהָא קָא מִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the משנה quoted in step 19 relates to שמואל's ruling.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's ruling that a שרץ itself brought into the מקדש is פטור
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהודה's reason, 'so as not to add טומאה', read as implying there is no חיוב

steps.title: Both agree it is חייב; they weigh delay against adding טומאה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the link. Everyone may hold that bringing in a שרץ is חייב. They only disagree about which is worse: leaving the טומאה longer, or adding more טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone agrees he is חייב. Here they disagree about this: one master holds that delaying the removal of the טומאה is the greater concern, and the other master holds that adding more טומאה is the greater concern.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the suggested proof. It shows that the משנה's dispute can be explained without touching the question of חייב or פטור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The debate is not about whether bringing in a שרץ is a sin. It is only about priorities when removing it. רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה cares more about speed, while רבי יהודה cares more about not creating new טומאה. So this משנה gives no evidence for or against שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
Leaving the טומאה in place longer
Increasing the amount of טומאה
Is weightier, takes priority

phrases.english: No, everyone agrees he is liable.
And here this is what they disagree about:
One master holds: the concern of delaying impurity is weightier.
And the other master holds: the concern of increasing impurity is weightier.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא חַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading proposed in step 20.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the link between the משנה and שמואל's ruling. It does not reject שמואל's ruling itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The dispute can be explained as a question of priorities in removing the שרץ, without either side holding פטור.

steps.title: Trying a different pair of תנאים in the same משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes that a different dispute in the same משנה, about which areas the שרץ must be removed from, matches the question of חייב or פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is like these other תנאים, as we learned in a משנה: From where do we take it out, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new attempt. It points to another dispute in the same משנה, about which areas of the מקדש the שרץ must be removed from, and will explain the connection next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the first pair of תנאים did not work, the גמרא moves to a different disagreement. That dispute is about whether the שרץ must be removed from all of the עזרה or only from the inner areas. The details of the parallel are filled in after this line.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the earlier suggestion and offers a new one)
Like these other תנאים
From which areas must it be removed

phrases.english: Rather, it is like these Tannaim, as we learned in a Mishnah:
From where do we take it out, etc.
phrases.notes: The rest of this משנה dispute (רבי שמעון בן ננס and רבי עקיבא) is analyzed next.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא כְּהָנֵי תַּנָּאֵי, דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the first parallel in step 21, the גמרא offers a different pair of תנאים.
steps.raayaObject: Whether bringing a שרץ into the מקדש is חייב, as discussed in שמואל's ruling
steps.raayaSupportSource: The dispute in the same משנה about which areas the שרץ must be removed from

steps.title: Linking the removal-area dispute to חייב or פטור
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the two תנאים disagree about the area of removal because they disagree about whether one who brings a שרץ into the מקדש is חייב or פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it that this is what they disagree about? The one who said we do not remove it from the עזרה holds that one who brings a שרץ into the מקדש is פטור. The one who said we remove it from the entire עזרה holds that he is חייב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains exactly how the dispute it raised in Step 22 connects to our question. Each side's view about where the שרץ must be removed from comes from its view on whether bringing a שרץ in is punishable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Removing a שרץ on שבת is only justified where leaving it there would involve a real violation. If bringing a שרץ into the עזרה carries no liability (פטור), there is no reason to remove it from the עזרה on שבת. If it does carry liability (חייב), it must be removed from the whole עזרה. If this reading holds, שמואל's ruling depends on a dispute between תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Isn't it that…?' A formula the גמרא uses to propose an explanation or proof
The Temple courtyard
One who brings a dead creeping creature into the Temple
'He holds' — introduces the reasoning behind someone's view
Exempt / liable to punishment

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume the proof is final. 'מַאי לָאו' only proposes a link, and the גמרא often goes on to reject it.
steps.whyThisMatters: If the link holds, שמואל's view is not a simple ruling. It is one side of a dispute between תנאים.

phrases.english: Isn't it that they disagree about this:
that the one who said 'not from the courtyard'
holds: one who brings a creeping creature into the Temple is exempt
phrases.notes: So there is no need to remove it from the courtyard on שבת.

phrases.english: and the one who said 'from the entire courtyard'
holds: he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי לָאו, בְּהָא קָא מִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proposal from Step 22 by spelling out which side holds חייב and which holds פטור.
steps.raayaObject: That whether bringing a שרץ into the מקדש is חייב or פטור is the subject of a dispute between תנאים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's dispute over whether a שרץ is removed from the עזרה on שבת or only from the inner areas
